label: live-window
execution_note: This file is recipe data, not a measurement. No seat executed, is permitted to execute, or did execute any step. L1/parent executes after the wave settles; each step records its own observed rc/digests into the manifest at run time. Any execution writes only under evidence_root.

tool_contract.interface_source: round-16 shared contract (wave1-spec context), not observed code
internal_query_forbidden: --after-cursor (only --cursor with exact-retained first record proves continuity)
tool_contract.expected_stdout: one JSON object: finding_id MORI_JOURNAL_WINDOW_OK on rc0, MORI_JOURNAL_WINDOW_UNAVAILABLE on rc2 unavailable, MORI_JOURNAL_WINDOW_SETUP on rc2 setup; raw cursor and raw records never echoed; anchor SHA-256 permitted
expected_internal_checks: first parsed record __CURSOR == anchor cursor exactly AND _BOOT_ID == anchor boot_id; that record is dropped, not counted
every later record: JSON object, _BOOT_ID == anchor boot_id, unique valid scalar __CURSOR
malformed/empty stdout, missing/mismatched/duplicate cursor, foreign boot, nonzero rc, any stderr byte, timeout, byte overflow -> rc2 unavailable, never partial or zero totals
anchor file is read-only input; anchor is never advanced or rewritten; end_cursor may be reported but is not written back

journalctl.version_floor: systemd >= 243 (--no-tail, --output-fields, -o json, --cursor all present in observed journalctl --help on 261.2-1-arch, 2026-10-20)
journalctl.docs_basis: S014 journalctl(1) systemd 262; S015 systemd.journal-fields(7) systemd 262; recipe argv restricted to flags confirmed on the installed binary
journalctl.run_time_check: sha256 the resolved binary and `journalctl --version` first line into manifest.tools before any journal read

jq.observed_version: jaq 3.1.1 resolves as jq on this host
jq.use: anchor projection only; filter is jq/jaq compatible; any equivalent JSON projector MAY substitute if the validation rules are identical
jq.note: r15 receipts pinned MORI_JQ_BIN=/usr/bin/jq; if the harness honours MORI_JQ_BIN, pin it the same way

boot_id_source.access: read-only kernel interface already used by the census

timeout_wrapper.implementation: coreutils timeout -k 1 <seconds> OR an equivalent subprocess wall-clock bound that kills and reaps only the owned child
timeout_wrapper.observed: uutils coreutils (sha256sum 0.8.0) provides timeout on this host

limits.limits_note: Configured bounds, not measured latency. timeout/overflow must produce rc2 unavailable, never a partial count; Bounds fixture pack owns the refusal cases.

forbidden_globally: requesting MESSAGE or COMMAND in any --output-fields list
parsing, storing, or echoing MESSAGE text anywhere

persisting raw journal JSONL, raw anchor records, raw cursors, or producer stderr content anywhere in receipts; raw material lives only in the temporary in-lane workspace evidence/live-window/tmp/ and is deleted before the manifest is finalized
echoing raw __CURSOR values, raw record fields, or journalctl/tool stderr into the manifest or reports
writing or moving any file outside evidence_root
advancing the anchor, using --cursor-file, or mutating cursor state
writing journald configuration, restarting journald, vacuuming, or any host mutation
partial-upgrade installs (pacman transactions are paused host-wide)

steps.purpose: prove binaries exist and record versions/digests before any journal read
steps.on_missing_tool: record capability_absent in manifest and stop; absent tool is not a production bug (WindowHarness contract)

steps.purpose: read normalized current boot id for per-record validation
steps.on_fail: both scopes unavailable:boot-id-unreadable; stop before any journal read
writes: manifest.boot_id (normalized 32-hex kernel boot id; safe, present in every record)

steps.purpose: acquire the LATEST anchor for scope=user: the record cursor of the newest retained current-boot entry, field-limited JSON
steps.anchor_source_rationale: the anchor is taken from the newest record's own __CURSOR inside the JSON object: it avoids parsing human-formatted cursor output and binds the anchor to that record's _BOOT_ID in the same object. --show-cursor/--cursor-file are not used (and --cursor-file is forbidden): the tool requires the first --cursor record to equal the anchor exactly, and a position emitted after the listing would not be that record's cursor

capture.stderr_file: evidence/live-window/tmp/anchor-user.stderr (count bytes then delete; content is never stored)

steps.expected_record_shape: one JSON object line containing only __CURSOR, __REALTIME_TIMESTAMP, __MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP, _BOOT_ID (the last four are always printed in field modes per S014 --output-fields)
validation: rc == 0 AND stderr byte count == 0 AND stdout bytes <= anchor_stdout_max_bytes AND timeout did not fire, else anchor unavailable for this scope
stdout is exactly one line that parses as a JSON object, else unavailable
.__CURSOR is a JSON string, length <= 4096 chars, printable with no control characters, else unavailable
._BOOT_ID is a JSON string matching ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ AND equals normalized boot_id from S01, else unavailable (foreign/older boot data is a boundary, not a fallback cue)
no MESSAGE key anywhere in the raw capture (assertion, not a read of its value)
steps.on_fail: record scope=user unavailable:<reason> in manifest; do NOT write an anchor file; do NOT run S03 for this scope; never retry with a different record

steps.purpose: project the validated record into schema mori-journal-anchor-v1
steps.write_policy: write to tmp/anchor-user.json.tmp then atomic mv; noclobber if tmp/anchor-user.json already exists; mode 0600; anchor JSON is temporary in-lane input, deleted at S04 — receipts retain only anchor_sha256 and boot_id
post_validation: re-read written file: schema == mori-journal-anchor-v1, scope == user, boot_id matches regex and S01 value, cursor scalar <=4096 printable
record anchor_sha256 = SHA-256 of written bytes in manifest (raw cursor never recorded)

steps.scope_access_note: system journal may be unreadable for this user (S014 access rules); rc!=0, stderr bytes, or empty stdout => unavailable, not zero

capture.stderr_file: evidence/live-window/tmp/anchor-system.stderr (count bytes then delete; content is never stored)

steps.purpose: project validated system record into mori-journal-anchor-v1
steps.write_policy: tmp-then-mv, noclobber, mode 0600; temporary in-lane, deleted at S04

steps.purpose: bounded same-boot new-since-anchor window observation, scope=user
steps.run_condition: only if S02b-anchor-user-write produced a validated anchor

capture.stdout_file: evidence/live-window/window-user.stdout.json (safe tool JSON: digests, ids, counts only — contract guarantees no cursor/record echo)
capture.stderr_file: evidence/live-window/tmp/window-user.stderr (count bytes then delete; content is never stored)

expected.rc0: finding_id=MORI_JOURNAL_WINDOW_OK; fields scope, records_after_anchor, positive_kernel_oom, positive_unit_oom, positive_unit_signal, positive_process_sigkill, evidence_basis=validated-record-subsets; optional end_cursor reported but never persisted
expected.rc2_unavailable: finding_id=MORI_JOURNAL_WINDOW_UNAVAILABLE with stable reason: missing/vacuumed anchor, boot boundary, malformed/empty/truncated/overflowing capture, foreign boot, nonzero producer rc, stderr bytes, timeout
expected.rc2_setup: finding_id=MORI_JOURNAL_WINDOW_SETUP for invalid anchor file or argv
expected.no_positive_totals: any unavailable MUST NOT carry numeric positive totals

manifest_record.positive_counts: four integers if rc0 else null
manifest_record.redacted: no cursor, no record payload, no reason strings beyond stable finding ids/reasons

steps.purpose: bounded same-boot new-since-anchor window observation, scope=system
steps.run_condition: only if S02b-anchor-system-write produced a validated anchor

capture.stdout_file: evidence/live-window/window-system.stdout.json (safe tool JSON: digests, ids, counts only)
capture.stderr_file: evidence/live-window/tmp/window-system.stderr (count bytes then delete; content is never stored)

fields.label: live-window
fields.recipe_sha256: SHA-256 of this capture-recipe.json at run start
fields.boot_id: normalized 32-hex kernel boot id observed for this run (safe: present in every record's _BOOT_ID)
fields.temporary_workspace_cleanup: BEFORE writing this manifest, delete evidence/live-window/tmp/ (raw anchor captures, anchor JSON inputs, stderr count files); assert the directory is absent or empty; raw anchor material is never committed or retained
invariants_checked: no MESSAGE key or value may appear in any evidence file; the grep check '"MESSAGE"' over evidence/live-window MUST return nothing (allowed field list makes even the key absent)
no raw cursor anywhere in run-manifest.json or evidence files
temporary workspace absent/empty at manifest time; only anchor_sha256 + boot_id + safe aggregates persist

steps.purpose: assert the committed receipt surface is digests and safe aggregates only
steps.note: anchor JSON files are consumed tool inputs, not receipts; their SHA-256 and boot_id are the only anchor facts retained

interpretation_boundaries.records_after_anchor: count of validated same-boot records strictly after the exact retained anchor; NOT a class total, NOT an event count, NOT deduplicated
interpretation_boundaries.positive_tokens: validated-record-subset witnesses per r15 predicates; never victim counts, never emitter-authenticated, never summed across scopes
interpretation_boundaries.unavailable: anchor vacuum/rotation between S02 and S03, foreign-boot records, capture failure and truncation all remain unavailable by design; FR11 advances only on exact cursor continuity
